brief.headline: HBM4E sampling accelerates, DRAM/NAND pricing decelerates from Q1 peak, hyperscaler capex guidance revised to $725B for 2026
brief.summary: <cite index="3-9">SK Hynix shipped 12-layer HBM4E samples to major customers in June 2026</cite>, while <cite index="8-7,8-10">Samsung began commercial HBM4 mass production in February with 11.7Gbps transfer speed and anticipates HBM sales to more than triple in 2026 versus 2025</cite>. <cite index="10-1">Conventional DRAM contract prices are projected to rise 13–18% QoQ in Q3 2026, with NAND up 10–15%—a marked deceleration from Q1's 90–95% DRAM surge and Q2's 58–63% increase</cite>. <cite index="20-6,21-15">The four largest hyperscalers plan $725 billion in combined 2026 capex, up 77% from $410 billion in 2025</cite>, while <cite index="31-10">CoWoS supply-demand gap is expected to narrow from ~20% currently to ~10% by end-2026</cite>. Both Korean names closed sharply higher today after Monday's steep selloff.
brief.pair_trade_view: SK Hynix remains structurally long. <cite index="4-11,4-12">SK Hynix holds 62% HBM shipment share as of Q2 2025 and 57% revenue share in Q3, with Goldman assessing the company will maintain dominant position in HBM3/HBM3E through at least 2026 and sustain total HBM market share over 50%</cite>. <cite index="4-17">UBS predicts SK Hynix will achieve ~70% market share in HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026</cite>. Samsung's HBM4 qualification momentum is improving but remains behind on 12-layer scale. <cite index="2-20,2-21">Samsung received favorable feedback in Nvidia HBM4 SiP tests while SK Hynix has already established HBM4 mass production framework and supplied paid samples to Nvidia</cite>. Near-term relative valuation spread has widened post-SK Hynix $26.5B Nasdaq ADR debut last week; Samsung exploring but has not committed to US listing. Pair remains long SK Hynix / short Samsung on HBM execution delta and 2H26–1H27 gross margin trajectory.

memory_cycle.stage: Late mid-cycle expansion, pricing momentum decelerating but elevated
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="12-10">Q1 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93–98% QoQ—buyers paid roughly double versus three months prior</cite>. <cite index="10-1">Q3 2026 DRAM contract price forecast of +13–18% QoQ and NAND +10–15% QoQ represents substantial deceleration from prior quarters</cite>. <cite index="12-19,12-21">AI-driven pull on high-capacity server DRAM and enterprise SSDs hasn't flinched, and HBM remains the tightest allocation-controlled product consuming wafer capacity that would otherwise produce commodity DRAM</cite>. <cite index="17-39,17-40">Gartner's Atwal states price will remain high almost through end of 2027, while Counterpoint places earliest inflection at Q4 2027 and Intel CEO Tan expects no relief until 2028</cite>. Supply response constrained by 2+ year fab lead times.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="3-10,3-11">SK Hynix's 12-layer HBM4E features 16Gbps per pin max data speed and power efficiency up over 20% versus previous models</cite>. <cite index="2-10,2-11">Nvidia has asked major memory suppliers whether they could deliver 16-layer HBM in Q4 2026, with discussions remaining exploratory but triggering internal planning around development schedules and yield targets</cite>. <cite index="4-7,4-9">HBM3E is expected to remain flagship product in 2026 HBM market; major analysts expect HBM3E to account for ~two-thirds of total HBM shipments in 2026 while HBM4 gradually increases share</cite>. <cite index="7-2,7-12">As Samsung and SK Hynix prioritize ramping HBM4, HBM3E supply remains tight and continues to lag demand; analysts forecast next year's HBM revenue mix at ~55% HBM4 and 45% HBM3E with HBM4 beginning in Q3 to rapidly absorb prior HBM3E demand</cite>. <cite index="2-5,2-6">HBM3E will account for 66% of total HBM output in 2026 per LS Securities estimates</cite>. 16-layer HBM4/HBM4E represents next inflection but faces thermal/bonding material thickness constraints within 775μm JEDEC standard.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix ships 12-layer HBM4E samples to major customers, 48GB capacity with Advanced MR-MUF tech
news_pulse.implication: Accelerates HBM roadmap; 17% heat resistance improvement vs HBM4 enables stable HPC operation. On schedule for timely mass production per customer engagement.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung begins HBM4 commercial mass production, ships first units with 11.7Gbps stable speed
news_pulse.implication: Industry-first mass production secures early HBM4 market leadership position. Samsung expects HBM sales to >3x in 2026 vs 2025; HBM4E sampling targeted 2H26.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia requests 16-layer HBM delivery by Q4 2026 from Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron
news_pulse.implication: Pulls forward generational transition before 12-layer HBM4 reaches full commercial rollout. Increases technical complexity and favors suppliers with proven stacking/thermal mgmt.

news_pulse.headline: Q3 2026 DRAM contract prices +13–18% QoQ, NAND +10–15% QoQ—sharp deceleration from Q1/Q2
news_pulse.implication: Parabolic phase maturing but not peaked. Consumer demand weakening; server DRAM partially capped by long-term agreements. Pricing power remains but momentum slowing.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex guidance revised to $725B, up 77% YoY from $410B in 2025
news_pulse.implication: AI infrastructure spend acceleration continues. Roughly 75% allocated to GPUs, high-bandwidth servers, networking, purpose-built data centers—direct HBM/DRAM demand driver.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from ~20% to ~10% by end-2026 as capacity expands
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS bottleneck easing. TSMC CoWoS capacity projected 120K–130K wpm by end-2026 vs 13K wpm end-2023. Improved advanced packaging supply supports HBM integration and GPU ramps.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix ADR (SKHY) surges 27% overnight, Korean shares +13% today after Monday 9% selloff
news_pulse.implication: Leveraged ETF launch (SKHU, SKUU, SKDD) amplifies volatility. Barclays initiates with $330 PT (+71% upside). Samsung +8% today; sector sentiment whipsaw post-US inflation data.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix CEO Kwak expects worst-ever global memory supply shortage in 2027, demand exceeds capacity past 2030
news_pulse.implication: Structural undersupply thesis reinforced. SK Hynix announces 100 trillion won ($64.4B) investment: 80T for M17 NAND fab (ops target 1H29), 20T for P&T7 advanced packaging facility.

brief.derivatives_signal: Elevated vol post-SK Hynix Nasdaq debut. SKHY full-chain put/call ratio 0.98 suggests two-sided hedging into surge rather than one-way call chasing. New 2x leveraged single-stock ETFs (SKHU, SKUU, SKDD) launched this week amplify intraday moves; ADR premium vs KRX-listed shares can snap back quickly. Kospi experienced extreme volatility: -9% Monday, +5.8% prior session, +8–13% today across Samsung/SK Hynix. Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) up 6% with 25% Samsung / 24% SK Hynix / 24% Micron concentration. Options flow favors near-dated structures around earnings and HBM qualification milestones. Watch SKHY–SKHY.KS ADR/local spread and Korean retail 'Ants' 3x leveraged ETF inflows for forced-selling risk.
